batches.title: CSV parser module (src/core/csv.js)
batches.description:
Create src/core/csv.js — CommonJS, only Node built-ins (no fs usage), exporting `module.exports = { parseCsv }`.

CONTRACT (pin all of it, invent nothing):
- Signature: `parseCsv(text) -> string[][]`. If `typeof text !== 'string'` throw `TypeError('parseCsv expects a string')`.
- Returns an array of rows; each row is an array of raw field strings (no trimming, no type conversion, no normalization).
- Line separators: both `\r\n` and `\n` terminate a record. A lone `\r` not followed by `\n` is NOT a separator and stays verbatim inside the field.
- Quoting: a field is quoted only when its first character is `"`; then everything up to the matching closing `"` is literal, including commas, `\r`, `\n`. Inside a quoted field `""` decodes to a single `"`. Text after the closing quote before the next separator is appended verbatim (no error). A `"` inside an unquoted field is kept verbatim.
- Empty/undefined handling: `parseCsv('')` -> `[]`. `parseCsv('\n')` -> `[]`. `parseCsv('\r\n')` -> `[]`. A line `a,,b` -> `['a','','b']`.
- Trailing empty lines: after splitting, DROP trailing rows that consist of exactly one empty field (the row produced by a final newline plus any extra blank lines at EOF). Interior blank lines are PRESERVED as a single-field row `['']`.
- Ragged rows are returned as-is (do not pad or normalize); the stats layer handles short rows.
- Unicode (e.g. Chinese) must be preserved byte-for-byte in the resulting strings; do not normalize or strip BOM-like characters except: if the text starts with `\uFEFF`, strip that single leading BOM before parsing (pin this).
- No external npm packages, no browser/Python APIs.

batches.title: Column statistics module (src/core/stats.js)
batches.description:
Create src/core/stats.js — CommonJS, only Node built-ins, exporting `module.exports = { columnStats }`.

CONTRACT (pin all of it, invent nothing):
- Signature: `columnStats(rows) -> Stat[]`. If `!Array.isArray(rows)` throw `TypeError('columnStats expects an array of rows')`.
- `rows[0]` is the HEADER and is excluded from every count. Column count = `rows[0].length`; the returned array has exactly that many entries with ascending `index` 0..n-1.
- If `rows.length === 0` return `[]`.
- `total` per column = `Math.max(0, rows.length - 1)` for EVERY column (counts every data row, including rows where the value is empty or the field is absent).
- Value extraction for data row `r` and column `i`: `value = (i < r.length && typeof r[i] === 'string') ? r[i] : ''` (a missing field counts as an empty string). `trimmed = value.trim()` (JS trim: removes spaces, tabs, and unicode whitespace).
- `missing` = count of data rows whose `trimmed === ''`.
- `type` = `'number'` iff (a) at least one non-empty trimmed value exists AND (b) every non-empty trimmed value satisfies `Number.isFinite(Number(trimmed))`; otherwise `'string'`. This literal rule means `'1e3'` -> 1000 numeric, `'0x10'` -> 16 numeric, `'Infinity'`/`'NaN'`/`'12abc'` -> non-numeric, and `''`/`'   '` are ignored (never the reason a column becomes non-numeric).
- Numeric columns: parse values with `Number(trimmed)`; `min` = `Math.min(...)` of parsed numbers, `max` = `Math.max(...)`, `mean` = `Math.round((sum / nonEmptyCount) * 100) / 100` where `nonEmptyCount` is the number of non-empty values and `sum` is the sum of parsed numbers. `unique` = `null` for numeric columns (PINNED: unique is only meaningful for string columns). If the rounded mean is `-0`, report it as `0`.
- String columns: `min`, `max`, `mean` are all `null`; `unique` = number of distinct non-empty trimmed values (a `Set` of trimmed values). This includes the all-empty case: type `'string'`, `unique` 0, `min`/`max`/`mean` null.
- Always return all 8 keys in this exact order: `{ index, type, total, missing, min, max, mean, unique }`. Never mutate `rows`. Integer counts must be plain JS numbers.
- No console output from this module. No external npm packages.

batches.title: Report renderer (src/report/report.js)
batches.description:
Create src/report/report.js — CommonJS, only Node built-ins, exporting `module.exports = { renderReport }`.

CONTRACT (pin all of it, invent nothing):
- Signature: `renderReport(rows) -> string`. It calls `columnStats` via `require('../core/stats.js')` (import as `const { columnStats } = require('../core/stats.js');`). It must NOT parse CSV and must NOT print anything — it only returns a string.
- Numeric column line (exact, no leading/trailing spaces): `col{index}: type=number total={total} missing={missing} min={min} max={max} mean={mean}`.
- String column line (exact): `col{index}: type=string total={total} missing={missing} unique={unique}`.
- Number formatting: `min` and `max` are written with plain `String(value)` (70 -> `70`, 3.5 -> `3.5`, -0 -> `0`). `mean` is written with `Number.prototype.toFixed(2)` (80 -> `80.00`, 2 -> `2.00`, 1.005 -> `1.00`); a rounded `-0` mean is normalized to `0` so it prints `0.00`.
- `total`, `missing`, `unique` are written as plain decimal integers via `String(n)` (unique here is the string-column unique; numeric lines never contain a `unique` field).
- Lines are joined with `'\n'` in ascending column index order; there is NO trailing newline and no blank line at the end. Each column produces exactly one line.
- Empty input: `renderReport([])` returns `''` (empty string, not `'\n'`).
- Deterministic: same input -> identical output; must not mutate `rows` and must not touch `process.exitCode`.
- No external npm packages; no console.log.

batches.title: CLI entrypoint (src/cli.js)
batches.description:
Create src/cli.js — CommonJS, only Node built-ins (`node:fs` or `fs`), exporting `module.exports = { run }`.

CONTRACT (pin all of it, invent nothing):
- Signature: `run(argv) -> undefined`. `argv` is a full `process.argv`-shaped array; the CSV file path is `argv[2]`. The function must never throw for the two error paths below; it always returns `undefined`.
- Imports (exact paths): `const fs = require('node:fs');`, `const { parseCsv } = require('./core/csv.js');`, `const { columnStats } = require('./core/stats.js');`, `const { renderReport } = require('./report/report.js');`.
- Missing argument: if `argv[2]` is `undefined` or `''` (after no trimming beyond that check) -> `console.error('Usage: node src/cli.js <csv-file>')` and set `process.exitCode = 1`; print nothing to stdout.
- Read error (ENOENT, EISDIR, permissions, any throw from `fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8')`) -> `console.error('Error: cannot read file: ' + path)` and set `process.exitCode = 1`; print nothing to stdout.
- Success path: `const rows = parseCsv(fs.readFileSync(argv[2], 'utf8')); const out = renderReport(columnStats(rows));` then `console.log(out)`. `process.exitCode` must be left untouched on success (the caller's 0 / undefined stays).
- STDOUT carries the report only; all diagnostics go to STDERR (console.error). No extra banners, no timing output.
- Auto-execution: at the bottom of the file exactly `if (require.main === module) { run(process.argv); }` — requiring this module must produce no output and must not set exitCode.
- Calls must be repeatable: no module-level mutable state; `run` must not cache file contents between calls.
- Do not create or modify package.json, lockfiles or .env.

batches.title: Sample data fixtures for smoke runs
batches.description:
Create exactly two files at the repository root, with EXACT byte content (the smoke runner feeds these to the CLI):

1) `sample-data.csv` — LF (`\n`) line endings, with a trailing newline:
```
name,score,note
Alice,90,good
Bob,80,"hello, world"
陈伟,70,
```
(The third data row has an empty `note` field; the middle row's `note` is quoted because it contains a comma; Chinese characters must be written as UTF-8 bytes.)
Expected derived output: `col0` string total=3 missing=0 unique=3; `col1` number total=3 missing=0 min=70 max=90 mean=80.00; `col2` string total=3 missing=1 unique=2.

2) `sample-edge.csv` — CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings everywhere, WITH a trailing CRLF, containing one quoted comma, one escaped-quote pair, and one quoted field containing a literal LF (`\n`):
```
id,label\r\n1,"a,b"\r\n2,"say ""hi"""\r\n3,"line1\nline2"\r\n```
(So: line 1 `id,label`; line 2 `1,"a,b"`; line 3 `2,"say ""hi"""`; line 4 `3,"line1` + a literal LF + `line2"`; then the final CRLF. Write the literal LF inside the quotes as a single `\n` byte, not CRLF.)
Expected derived output: exactly 3 data rows (the trailing CRLF must NOT add a row); `col0` number total=3 missing=0 min=1 max=3 mean=2.00; `col1` string total=3 missing=0 unique=3.

Rules: these files must contain no BOM, no header comment lines, and no extra trailing blank lines beyond the one stated. Do not touch any other file or directory.
